previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, and cardiomyopathy due to Chagas disease presented with fever, nausea, vomiting, and diffuse abdominal pain. He was found to have MSSA bacteremia originating from an infected left arm AV graft, which showed signs of cellulitis. Blood and wound cultures confirmed methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus. He was started on vancomycin, then transitioned to cefazolin, and underwent removal of the infected graft. A temporary dialysis catheter was placed in the right external jugular vein, later converted to a tunneled catheter. Repeat blood cultures became negative, and his clinical condition improved. He was discharged home on a four-week course of IV cefazolin administered during dialysis, with close outpatient follow-up planned with infectious disease, transplant, and primary care teams.

#. Anemia. 

Patient found at ___ to have Hct of 28 which is 4 points down 
from his typical baseline. He also has an unclear history of 
possible black stool. He was transferred to ___ ED where he 
received 1 U PRBC prior to admission to the medicine service and 
his Hct bumped appropriately from 28 to 31.8 after transfusion. 
His story was not convincing for melena given that patient 
reports that secondary to his poor vision he is really unable to 
differentiate color variation in his stool. Further he was 
guaiac negative x2. Given his appropriate Hct bump and normal 
haptoglobin and bilirubin we thought hemolysis less likely. His 
iron studies, Vit B12 and folate studies did not point toward 
any deficiencies. On discharge we had not identified a source of 
bleeding and thought that his Hct drop could be possibly  be 
secondary to volume shifts on top of anemia of chronic illness 
given high ferritin. He should continue epo with HD and 
age-appropriate cancer screens. He would likely do well with a 
repeat colonoscopy as an outpatient to rule out intermittent 
intraluminal bleeding source; his last in ___ had normal 
random biopsies x 4 but was limited by suboptimal quality of the 
prep and one-year follow-up had been recommended.

#. ESRD.

Patient transferred directly from ___ and did not complete 
a full session of HD. He received 3hrs of HD here and will 
resume his ___ schedule upon discharge. Patient recently 
admitted for graft site infection on the left and now with 
tunnelled IJ. His old site and new site both look intact and 
free of infection. 
.
#. Depression.
When discussing with team, patient's wife expressed concern that 
patient is having worsening depression. Patient is not taking 
his mirtazapine as directed as it makes him drowsy. Mrs ___ 
describes patient's symptoms of depression in the following way: 
problems with sleep and often restless; decreased energy 
compared to prior baselines; less reactive mood except when with 
grandchildren; decreased appetite. Patient would likely benefit 
from trial of a non-sedating anti-depressant. TSH nl in ___.

Discharge Instructions:
It was a pleasure taking care of you here at the ___.

You came to the Emergency Department because while at 
hemodialysis you were noted to be weak and you also had a slight 
drop in your red blood cell count. In the Emergency Department 
you received 1 unit of red blood cells and your red blood cell 
count responded appropriately to this. We think that you might 
have had fluid overload causing your red blood cell count to 
look lower than it normal does. You received hemodialysis while 
here with us because you did not fully receive dialysis prior to 
coming to us.

You also mentioned to us that you might have had an episode of 
dark stool a few days ago. There a number of reasons for dark 
stool including bleeding in your abdomen. On this admission it 
did not appear that you were actively bleeding but you should 
discuss with your primary care physician about whether you 
should have an outpatient colonoscopy.

You should also weigh yourself every morning and call your PCP 
if weight goes up more than 3 lbs.

We made no changes to your medications.
